case.provenance: New synthetic regression case for ANY-761; not an original QA output.

input.brief_text: We need two files for Acme: PDF and JSON. Both files must contain the exact string "Ready to ship". Deadline: November 15. Budget: 500 EUR. We assume the source data has already been provided.
input.deliverable_text: Only the PDF for Acme with the string "Ready to ship" has been delivered. JSON has not been delivered. The deadline and budget were met.

criteria: Every authored canonical field follows the expected analysis language, including summaries and evidence explanations.
Quotations, brands, technical identifiers, source dates and amounts stay faithful; identifiers and enums are unchanged.
No invented facts, hidden findings, changed verdicts or unsupported readiness claims.

document.summary: The work does not meet expectations because the required JSON file is missing. The first priority is to deliver the JSON file for Acme containing the exact string "Ready to ship".

sections.title: Verdict
sections.content:
The work does not meet expectations. This verdict is based on the four general review criteria, not an item-by-item assessment of the acceptance criteria listed below.
Scope coverage is not satisfied: the brief requires PDF and JSON files for Acme, but the delivery states that only the PDF was delivered and that JSON has not been delivered.
Requirement fit is not satisfied: both files must contain the exact string "Ready to ship"; the delivered PDF is reported to contain it, but the required JSON is absent. The delivery states that the deadline and budget were met.
Completeness is not satisfied: the brief lists two required files, PDF and JSON, and the delivery explicitly confirms that JSON has not been delivered.
Clarity is satisfied: the delivery plainly identifies what was delivered—the PDF with "Ready to ship"—and what was not—the JSON. It also states that the deadline and budget were met.
